newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index seen pushing closer to 3,000 pts.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index seen pushing closer to 3,000 pts.

text.p: Germany's DAX-30 top share index was seen pushing closer to 3,000 points on Tuesday after U.S. consumer price data came in according to forecasts, easing yet further the lingering fears of a U.S. interest rate hike.

The IBIS-DAX electronic trade index had by late-session climbed 26.16 points in post-bourse trade to 2,982.94, just off a record-high reached earlier of 2,984.32. March DAX futures rose 26 points to hit a record 3,000 points.
"Unless there are any upsets from the U.S., I think we can reach the 3,000 points (in the cash index) this week now," said one trader.
"The dollar is strong, the bond market is friendly -- the whole background is positive now," he said.

U.S. consumer price data, among the clearest indicators of the country's inflationary trends, had earlier shown a 0.3 percent rise in December, exactly in line with the consensus of economist forecasts.
Dealers said the data cut the chances of a consolidation on the German market before it attempted to scale 3,000 points.
Among individual shares, airline Lufthansa's sharp fall after a new draft share ownership law was among the most marked movements.

Aviation analysts said the fall, which at one point took Lufthansa stock some 5.7 percent lower in bourse trade, was overdone in that it need not in practice have any impact on international investors' holdings in Lufthansa.
Indeed, in as much as the draft laws would speed the completion of Lufthansa's privatisation later this year, they were in the long-run positive for the share price, they noted.
Elsewhere, German building stocks fell after the downbeat sector forecast from the BI industry grouping on Monday.
Holzmann lost 10 marks to 370 in IBIS trade, while Bilfinger+Berger fell 1.20 marks to 59.80.

Shares in sportswear-maker Adidas AG fell four marks to 137 as dealers said the stock reacted in sympathy with earlier weakness in the shares of its rival Puma, which by Tuesday was trading 1.30 marks up at 52.50.
Traders noted the movements were largely technical, with no fundamental significance.
